paraphrase: The lineage (gotra) of a disciple is the seed of the qualities of liberation already present; one who has it can attain nirvāṇa given the right conditions — human birth, a central land, intact faculties, faith, the appearance of a buddha, the teaching and a spiritual friend.

paraphrase: The objects that purify conduct are prescribed by temperament: the unattractive for one of lustful conduct, loving-kindness for the hateful, dependent origination for the deluded, the analysis of the elements for the proud, and mindfulness of breathing for the discursive.

paraphrase: The limit of things (vastuparyantatā) is their extent — everything conditioned summed up in the five aggregates, all dharmas in the elements and bases, all knowables in the noble truths — and their reality, suchness, established by four kinds of reasoning: of dependence, of efficacy, of valid proof, and of the nature of things.

paraphrase: Insight is fourfold: a monk discerns dharmas, investigates them thoroughly, considers them and examines them — with respect to their extent and their reality.

paraphrase: By the ninefold settling of the mind one settles the mind inwardly: one places it, settles it firmly, re-settles it, settles it closely, tames it, calms it, calms it fully, makes it one-pointed and brings it to concentration. These are accomplished by six powers — hearing, reflection, mindfulness, awareness, vigour and familiarity — and accompanied by four attentions: forced, interrupted, uninterrupted and spontaneous.

paraphrase: When calm is attained, pliancy of mind arises, and with it pliancy of body: the badness (dauṣṭhulya) that makes body and mind unworkable is removed, and a lightness is felt, as if in the head, spreading through the body.
notes: Recalled from the Śrāvakabhūmi's account of the arising of pliancy; not located in the e-text in this pass.

paraphrase: The yogin reaches freedom from desire for sense-pleasures by seven attentions: the attention discerning characteristics, that arising from resolve, that of seclusion, that gathering delight, that of examination, that of the completion of practice, and that which is the fruit of the completion of practice; the first discerns the coarseness of sense-pleasures and the peace of the first absorption.
